messages.subject: Hold out test on BYM
parts:

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Hold out test on BYM
parts:
leave-out-one-at-the-time is there already. If you want to leave out
more, you can do that in the loop, and set a selection of theresponse
to NA. recall to set them back afterwards. this will create predictions
for the ones you leave out.

if you look at the code for

inla.cpo

you can use the control.mode=list(result=r, restart=T)

trick to make it run a bit faster, and also you can turn off to compute
those marginals you will not need.

btw, it is not possible to see what is wrong with the call below,as its
all in the indices.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Hold out test on BYM
parts:
Again, there’s far too little information.
If the estimated dependence is small, than the predictions will essentially be the common mean. For some problems, variations in the decimals can be highly significant. For others, less so. The estimates need to be taken I context, and not only the means but also the std.dev. and quantiles are informative. You need to show more of the actual numbers and parameter estimates.

Finn
